```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the get-started vignette:
# the source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a
# bare installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Every plotting face of the package on one page, organized by the question
each figure answers. One small simulated cohort drives the whole gallery:
the setup block draws it with `ms_simulate()`, then runs the fast faces --
`ms_fit()` for reference exposures, `ms_extract()` for de-novo signatures,
plus the bootstrap, stratification, embedding and QC surfaces -- so every
figure below reuses the same `MsCatalog`, `MsSignature` and `MsFit`
objects. The variant-to-catalog face (`ms_tally()`) is not needed here; it
is covered in [get-started.html](get-started.html). Each example opens
with the situation the figure is for; all faces return ggplot objects, so
anything shown can be re-themed or extended with the usual ggplot2 layers.

## One cohort for the whole gallery

The dictionary is sliced from the bundled COSMIC reference face, whose
matrices already carry the canonical SBS96 channel labels.

```{r dictionary}
refdb <- ms_refdb_bundled(build = "GRCh38")
sbs <- refdb[["SBS_GRCh38"]]@matrices[[1]]
dict <- sbs[, c("SBS1", "SBS5", "SBS13", "SBS57")]
```

The cohort plants a clock-like pair everywhere, an APOBEC signature in a
subgroup, the artifact signature SBS57 in another subgroup, and one
deliberately hypermutated member that rides a count-scale exposure column
instead of a share column.

```{r cohort}
samples <- c(paste0("T", 1:12), "H1")
act <- matrix(0, nrow = ncol(dict), ncol = length(samples),
              dimnames = list(colnames(dict), samples))
act["SBS1", samples[1:12]] <- 0.50
act["SBS5", samples[1:12]] <- 0.42
act["SBS13", c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4")] <- 0.08
act["SBS57", c("T5", "T6")] <- 0.08
resid <- 1 - colSums(act[, samples[1:12]])
act["SBS1", samples[1:12]] <- act["SBS1", samples[1:12]] + resid / 2
act["SBS5", samples[1:12]] <- act["SBS5", samples[1:12]] + resid / 2
act["SBS1", "H1"] <- 12500
act["SBS5", "H1"] <- 10000
act["SBS13", "H1"] <- 2500
cat <- ms_simulate(dict, act, burden = 600, seed = 14)
cat
```

The reused objects, all at minimal settings so the page renders quickly
(the de-novo face uses a single seeded NMF engine; `ms_extract()`'s
default consensus pipeline and the bootstrap's default replicate count
are the thorough settings for real analyses).

```{r objects}
fit <- ms_fit(cat, dict)
sig <- ms_extract(cat, k = 3, method = "nmf")
boot <- ms_fit_bootstrap(cat, dict, method = "nnls", n_boot = 50, seed = 1,
                         return_draws = TRUE)
strat <- ms_stratify_hypermutants(cat, seed = 1)
emb <- ms_embed(fit@exposures, method = "kmeans", clusters = 2L, seed = 1)
qc <- ms_qc_report(cat, dict, fit@exposures)
roster <- ms_qc_roster_share(cat, dict, fit@exposures)
```

## Catalog and signature profiles

`plot_catalog_profile()` is for rendering a single profile column --
one catalog sample or one signature -- in the COSMIC bar style, with the
substitution classes colored and the flanking-context labels vertical.

```{r profile-sample, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3}
plot_catalog_profile(cat@counts, column = "T1")
```

In `mode = "count"` the y axis carries raw mutations instead of shares --
the natural reading for a burden outlier such as the hypermutated member.

```{r profile-hyper, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3}
plot_catalog_profile(cat@counts, column = "H1", mode = "count")
```

`plot_signature_catalog()` is for inspecting a whole signature set at
once: the same semantics, one panel per signature. It accepts a matrix or
an `MsSignature` directly.

```{r signature-catalog, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3}
plot_signature_catalog(sig)
```

## Reference comparison

`plot_cosmic_scatter()` is for judging, channel by channel, how an
estimated profile lines up against a reference profile: the identity
line, the cosine, and an empirical signature-null tail probability are
annotated on the plot itself.

```{r cosmic-scatter, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4, message = FALSE}
plot_cosmic_scatter(sig@signatures[, 1], dict[, "SBS1"], label = "SBS1")
```

`plot_reference_comparison()` is for the same pairing when the deviations
matter more than the summary: the estimate is drawn dark and the
reference light, on shared axes.

```{r reference-comparison, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3, message = FALSE}
plot_reference_comparison(sig@signatures[, 1], dict[, "SBS1"])
```

## Exposure structure

`plot_exposure_heatmap()` is for reading the cohort-wide exposure matrix
at a glance, one row per sample; the exposure faces accept the labelled
matrix or an `MsSignature`.

```{r exposure-heatmap, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4}
plot_exposure_heatmap(fit@exposures)
```

`plot_exposure_stacked()` is for the compositional story per sample: one
bar per sample, stacked by signature share.

```{r exposure-stacked, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
plot_exposure_stacked(fit@exposures)
```

`plot_exposure_riverplot()` is for the same table read as flows between
the sample axis and the signature axis (requires the ggalluvial package).

```{r exposure-riverplot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
plot_exposure_riverplot(fit@exposures)
```

## Evidence panels

`plot_boot_ci()` is for a single sample's decomposition with uncertainty
bars: point exposures with their bootstrap percentile whiskers, ordered
by exposure share.

```{r boot-ci, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_boot_ci(boot, sample = "H1")
```

`plot_boot_distribution()` is for the shape of the resampling evidence
itself, not just the interval endpoints: per-signature histograms of the
raw boot draws, with the estimate and both bounds marked (the fit must
carry the draws cube, hence `return_draws = TRUE` above).

```{r boot-distribution, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
plot_boot_distribution(boot, sample = "T1")
```

`plot_hypermutator_burden()` is for seeing who was flagged as
hypermutated: a burden histogram colored by the stored adjudication, with
the stored cutoff as a dashed line -- nothing is re-thresholded at plot
time.

```{r hypermutator-burden, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_hypermutator_burden(strat)
```

`plot_embedding()` is for seeing how samples organize in exposure space;
when the embedding table carries a cluster column the points are colored
by it.

```{r embedding, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4}
plot_embedding(emb)
```

## QC

`plot_qc_dashboard()` is for reading per-sample burden and the artifact
sentries on one shared sample axis, drawn exactly as the QC report stored
them -- burden classes on the top panel, the G>T and C>T sentinel shares
below, colored by the stored flags.

```{r qc-dashboard, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
plot_qc_dashboard(qc)
```

`plot_pseudosig_contribution()` is for ranking the per-sample artifact
share of the exposure, with the contributing artifact signatures
labelled and the flagged samples colored by their verdict.

```{r pseudosig-contribution, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
plot_pseudosig_contribution(roster)
```

## Where to go next

The figures above draw what the certified faces stored; the statistics
behind the comparison machinery are the subject of [Comparing
signatures](comparing-signatures.html), and the QC surfaces themselves --
the report, the roster share and their flags -- are documented in
[Quality control](quality-control.html).
